issues.t: Fuel pump relay and rear fuse block melt
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or it stalls while driving and will not restart. Some owners notice a burning smell from under the rear seat.
issues.why: The fuel pump relay plugs into a fuse block under the rear seat. The relay can overheat and melt its socket, and a seat frame tab pressing on the fuse block cover has been blamed. GM issued a bulletin about the seat touching this fuse block.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If the car stalls or will not start, have the fuel pump relay and rear fuse block checked before replacing the fuel pump. A melted fuse block needs to be replaced, not just the relay.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails and engine stalls
issues.sym: The engine sputters, loses power, stalls and will not restart, or cranks a long time before it starts.
issues.why: The in-tank electric fuel pump wears out, and a failing relay or fuse block can also take the pump down with it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Stalling in traffic is dangerous, so get it checked right away. Have fuel pressure tested and the relay checked before buying a pump.

issues.t: Ignition key can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, often after the key ring is bumped or the road is rough. Power steering and power brakes get much heavier.
issues.why: A heavy key ring or a knee bump can turn the ignition out of Run. The airbags may then not deploy in a crash.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Take extra keys off the ring and have a Buick dealer check your VIN to make sure the recall was done.

issues.t: Heated washer fluid system can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the front of the car, or other electrical features acting up.
issues.why: The heated windshield washer module can short circuit and overheat. GM recalled it twice and later disabled the system.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN to confirm both recalls were done. Stop and turn the car off if you smell burning plastic.

issues.t: Power steering hose can fail and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Steering gets heavy at low speed, and fluid may drip near the engine.
issues.why: A power steering hose can fail. Fluid that lands on hot engine parts can start a fire.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Battery cable can rub a power steering line (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power steering assist and power steering fluid leaking in the engine bay.
issues.why: On some cars the battery cable was routed where it could wear a hole in a power steering line. Leaking fluid can also catch fire on hot parts.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for the recall. Do not keep driving with a power steering leak.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, delayed or harsh shifts, the car will not move in some gears, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic can wear out its clutches or have valve body and solenoid problems. Owners report failures from about 57,000 miles up.
issues.next: Have the fluid and codes checked when shifting changes. Early valve body or solenoid repairs can prevent the need for a rebuilt transmission.

issues.t: Head gasket failure and overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs on the highway or on hills, coolant keeps disappearing, white smoke from the tailpipe, or milky oil.
issues.why: The Northstar V8 is known for head gasket leaks, usually blamed on the head bolts losing their grip in the aluminum block. Once coolant gets into the cylinders the repair is a major job.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Have a cooling system and combustion leak test done. A full head gasket repair is a major job, so get a clear diagnosis first.

issues.t: Engine stalls from a failing crankshaft sensor or ignition module
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, often with the steering and brakes getting heavy, then may restart after a few minutes.
issues.why: Owners report stalling traced to the crankshaft position sensor, the ignition control module or coil connections. Stalling while driving is the most common engine complaint on later Lucernes.
issues.next: Have stored codes read as soon as it happens. If the fuel pump relay and rear fuse block check out, test the crank sensor and ignition parts next.

issues.t: Oil leaks and burning oil smell
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, smoke from under the hood, or oil spots under the engine.
issues.why: Gaskets and seals harden with age and let oil reach hot exhaust parts. On the Northstar V8, leaks from the lower engine seals can be a big job because the engine may need to come out.
issues.next: Have the leak found while it is small. Keep the oil level correct, and do not ignore smoke from under the hood.

issues.t: Shocks and struts leak or fail
issues.sym: A floaty or bouncy ride, clunks over bumps, oily residue on the shocks, or a suspension warning on CXS and Super models.
issues.why: The shocks and struts wear and leak. Models with magnetic ride control use electronic shocks, and GM issued bulletins for leaks and a loose shock connector.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected. If you have magnetic ride control, ask whether a connector repair fixes the warning before replacing shocks.

issues.t: Clunk in the steering when turning slowly
issues.sym: A clunk or bump felt in the steering wheel when turning at low speed, like in parking lots.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft that links the column to the steering gear wears. GM issued a bulletin to replace it.
issues.next: Most of the time this is a worn steering-shaft joint, but a clunk can also come from worn tie rods or ball joints, which are serious. Have the steering and front end checked soon, and sooner if the steering feels loose or the car wanders. Ask about the GM bulletin.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leaks
issues.sym: A whining pump, heavier steering, and red or amber fluid under the front of the car.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for leaks at the steering gear line connection and at the fluid reservoir.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the leak found. Running the pump low on fluid can ruin it.

issues.t: ABS, traction and StabiliTrak lights come on
issues.sym: The ABS and traction lights come on together, and the dash may say Service StabiliTrak.
issues.why: A wheel speed sensor, steering angle sensor or related wiring sends a bad signal, so the system shuts itself off. GM issued several bulletins for these codes.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but ABS and stability control may not. Have the codes read to find the faulty sensor.

issues.t: No crank, no start with the security light on
issues.sym: You turn the key and nothing happens, or the engine starts and dies, and the security light may be on.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for no-crank conditions caused by a voltage spike to the engine computer and by theft-deterrent problems.
issues.next: Have the battery tested first, then ask a shop to check the GM bulletins for no-crank with the security light on.

issues.t: No crank and dark gear display from damaged wiring
issues.sym: The car will not crank and the gear indicator (PRNDL) light is out.
issues.why: GM found that a wiring harness at the transmission could be damaged, cutting the signal that tells the car it is in Park.
issues.next: Have a shop check the transmission wiring harness and follow the GM bulletin.

issues.t: Reduced power and check engine light from the throttle body
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the car hesitates, and it may go into a reduced power mode.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body can get dirty or its sensors can fail. GM issued bulletins to inspect and service it.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning or replacing the throttle body usually fixes it.

issues.t: Intermittent check engine light and reduced power from a dash wiring connector
issues.sym: The check engine light comes and goes, and the car may briefly drop into reduced power.
issues.why: GM found poor connections at the wiring connector between the instrument panel and body harness.
issues.next: Ask the shop to check the GM bulletin for this connector before replacing sensors.

issues.t: Knock sensor codes and spark knock
issues.sym: Check engine light with knock sensor codes, pinging under load, or a slight misfire.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for knock sensor faults on the 3.8L V6.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the knock sensors and wiring checked.

issues.t: Engine mounts break
issues.sym: Heavy vibration at idle, a clunk when shifting into gear or when accelerating.
issues.why: Owners report engine mounts that fail repeatedly.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected if you feel a clunk. Worn mounts can stress hoses and wiring.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum
issues.sym: A humming or grinding noise from a front wheel that gets louder with speed.
issues.why: The sealed hub and bearing assemblies wear out.
issues.next: Have the hubs checked. Replace the noisy one before it gets loose.

issues.t: Corroded wheel rims leak air
issues.sym: One or more tires slowly lose air, and the tire pressure light comes on.
issues.why: Corrosion builds up where the tire bead seals against the alloy wheel.
issues.next: Have the shop clean the rim seat and reseal the tire. Badly corroded wheels may need to be refinished or replaced.
